posts:
We put the live score on a TV in a school sports hall.

Same match. Same teams. The parents in the stand behaved differently.

What actually changed:

Before, the score lived with the secretary at the desk.

Parents asked each other what it was. Players on the bench were not sure. Someone would shout "what's the score?" from the court and lose their position doing it.

After: a screen on the wall. Score, clock, latest events.

First thing we noticed — parents stopped leaving at half time. When you can see the score and how long is left, walking out is psychologically harder.

Second: behaviour on court changed.

A visible clock changes the game. Two minutes left with one goal in it plays very differently from "this will probably end soon".

You can see it with the naked eye.

Third, and unexpected: people started filming.

A shot with a scoreboard in the corner looks like a broadcast. The same shot without one looks like phone footage from a gym.

Parents filmed and posted it themselves. Free reach that did not exist before.

What it takes technically: a screen and a link.

TV, projector or a second laptop. The board opens in a browser. No dedicated hardware, no installation.

If your hall has anything you can put a picture on, try it for one match.

Cheapest atmosphere upgrade I have seen in school sport.
